prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your location in the Atlanta metro area, budget, system size, product preferences, and whether you want a national chain or a local business. I can, however, help you find the best contractor for your situation and give names and a checklist so you can pick confidently.

Quick options (commonly used by Atlanta homeowners)
- Coolray (regional company with a strong presence in metro Atlanta)
- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning (local franchise of a national company)
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (large regional provider with HVAC crews in Atlanta)
- Palmer Home Services (Atlanta-based home services company)
Note: these are examples of reputable providers that operate in the area. Always check current local reviews, licensing, and recent customer feedback before hiring.

How to choose the best contractor (step-by-step)
1. Get at least 3 written estimates:
   - Make sure each includes equipment brand/model, SEER rating, tonnage, labor, permit costs, and total price.  
2. Verify technical work:
   - Insist on a Manual J load calculation (proper sizing), Manual S equipment selection, and Manual D if ductwork is involved. Avoid companies that just size “by rule of thumb.”  
3. Confirm credentials:
   - Georgia HVAC license, EPA refrigerant certification, and NATE-certified technicians are strong positives. Also check business licenses and insurance.  
4. Warranty & service:
   - Ask about manufacturer and installer warranties, and what maintenance plans they offer. Get warranty terms in writing.  
5. Ask these questions:
   - Will you perform a load calculation? What size and SEER of system do you recommend and why? Who will do the installation (employees vs. subcontractors)? Are permits included? How long will the job take? What’s the payment schedule and financing options?  
6. Check reviews & references:
   - Look on Google, Yelp, BBB, Angi (formerly Angie’s List), and ask the contractor for recent local references.  
7. Watch for red flags:
   - Extremely low bids with vague scope, pressure to sign immediately, no written estimate, no permit work, or unwillingness to show credentials.

Ballpark cost and timing (Atlanta)
- Typical full replacement of a central AC (2–5 ton) including installation: roughly $4,000–$12,000 depending on equipment efficiency, ductwork needs, and complexity. High-efficiency or variable-speed systems cost more.  
- Typical install time: 1–3 days for a straight swap; longer if ductwork or zoning is needed.

If you want, I can:
- Help you draft an RFP/email to send to contractors.
- Provide a checklist to bring to on-site estimates.
- Look up and compare top-rated contractors in your specific ZIP code (share your ZIP and I’ll tailor recommendations and what to watch for locally).
